note: Tokens are keyed by PHYSICAL MATERIAL; parts reference them by alias or assignment. Values are copied byte-for-byte from the approved, locked material set — the port changes keying and grouping only. Entries sharing a `family` are the same substance: where their values differ that is an inconsistency for a human to reconcile, and validate-tokens.mjs reports it.

colorManagement.blenderParity: Blender must render ACES (not 'Standard') at this exposure. See docs/configurator/RENDER-DESIGN-SYSTEM-PROPOSAL.md §3.

glass.why: Glass carries per-geometry thickness bakes and approved per-colourway env rotations; porting it alongside the metals would have put two approved surfaces at risk in one change. Ported next.

polymer.pp.translucent.provenance: RENDERS VIA MATCAP (matcaps/diptube.png), not PBR: the tube is DRAWN BY ITS EDGES like Jordan's reference photo - two soft grey edge lines, core melted to the stage-through-glass tone, one faint sheen line. View-dependent, env-free (no rotation flare), opaque pass (visible through transmissive glass). Regenerate via the numpy recipe in the matcap commit. TRANSLUCENCY IS PAINTED, NOT SIMULATED: three's transmission buffer excludes transparent AND transmissive parts, so the tube must be opaque - and a translucent object READS as its background seen through milk. The PSD tube layer is near-white because the photo background is white; on OUR taupe stage the same tube reads milky-taupe #c9c0b4. Low env intensity kills the white rotation flare (Jordan). O2.8 curved thread per the product photos.
